title: Safety ladder — staged release playbook (personal notes)
content:
TL;DR:
Personal scratchpad for a safety-ladder approach to staged releases. Focused on minimal blast radius + automated attenuation + clear human handoff points. This is an iterating note — not the canonical runbook. Use for preflight and quick decision-making during rollouts.

Goals:
- Protect SLOs and user-facing latency while allowing small, measurable traffic to new model/serving changes.
- Make rollback/pin actions unambiguous and automatable.
- Bake in visibility and escalation hooks so anyone on-call can act without deep context.

Context / Constraints:
- Target environments: hosted-api (prod region-us-west1) and Dedicated pools (dedicated-pool-03).
- New artifact: model-id=redwood-7b-q2-opt-v3, runtime change: continuous-batching v2.2.
- Canaries must not exceed 3% global RPS for the first 2 hours unless gated.

Acceptance criteria for progressing to the next rung:
- No user-facing error rate regression >+0.15% absolute for 30m rolling.
- 95th p90 latency delta < +120ms for requests with length <512 tokens.
- No increase in token cost per 1k requests > +8% (sudden spike may indicate quantization/execution path regression).
- No new 5xx class errors attributable to the model or runtime (tracked via trace tags: rollout=as-safety-ladder).

Safety ladder (staged steps):
- Step 0 — Offline verification (dev/staging): run 3 deterministic sims and 10k sampled prompts through offline eval harness. Check outputs for semantic regressions via prompt set 'release-smoke-v2'.
- Step 1 — Shadow mode: route traffic to production runtime but do not serve responses; collect latencies, memory/KV pressure, and cost. Run for 1h.
- Step 2 — Tiny canary (0.5% RPS, max 100qps region): run 60–90 minutes. Immediate triggers for rollback: error delta or latency breach.
- Step 3 — Small canary (2% RPS): 2h sustained, allow scaling tests and autoscaler behavior (burst tests).
- Step 4 — Ramp (10%): monitor for emergent regressions, ensure fallback to a pinned variant if needed.
- Step 5 — Full rollout: only after 24h stable at 10% and sign-off via Slack + ticket closure.

Automated thresholds (monitoring):
- error_rate_5m_new - error_rate_5m_baseline > 0.0015 -> alert / auto-attenuate 75% of canary traffic
- p95_latency_delta_5m > 120ms -> alert + pause ramp for human review (pager if oncall)
- token_cost_delta_1h > 8% -> alert to infra-cost channel; if sustained 30m, attenuate
- memory_kv_pressure > 85% -> auto-offload new variant and route to fallback (pin)

Automated actions mapped to ladder rung breach:
- Auto-attenuate: cut canary traffic by 50% (API call: curl POST /internal/rollouts/attenuate?percent=50) and post to #prod-rollouts with context.
- Pin to previous: create emergency rollback PR template and run infra job to pin model-version=X immediately.
- If severe (5xx spike > 3% absolute) -> automated rollback + create incident (opsgenie) and notify on-call.

Human escalation flow (who does what):
- On-call engineer (first responder): verify metrics dashboard, scope issue (model vs runtime), attempt attenuation via one-click in console, post status in Slack.
- SE/owner (me): run quick regression test with 50 sample prompts, check logs for traceback correlation (kernel selection, quant path), decide pin or escalate to SRE.
- SRE: if infrastructure (GPU OOM, kernel crash), execute infra fallback and open infra incident.
- PM/Design: assess user-visible behavior and decide re-eval cadence for rollout.

Preflight checklist (tick-off before Step 2):
- [ ] Smoke run in staging completed (log + output diffs attached)
- [ ] Autoscaler tuning verified against synthetic burst (PR: #7890)
- [ ] Canary config uploaded (traffic policy, region list, prewarming nodes)
- [ ] Dashboards deployed with 'rollout=as-safety-ladder' filter
- [ ] Notification templates seeded in Slack + PagerDuty

Quick commands (personal notes):
- Attenuate 50% (canary id): curl -X POST $INTERNAL/rollouts/attenuate -d '{"canary":"as-2026-03","percent":50}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Pin model: ./scripts/pin_model.sh --model redwood-7b-q2-opt-v3 --to redwood-7b-q2-opt-v2
- Trigger emergency rollback job: airflow trigger_dag --conf '{"rollout":"as-2026-03","action":"rollback"}' emergency_rollback_dag

Observation notes to log after each rung (copy into ticket):
- timestamp, canary-id, region, rps, p50/p95/p99, error-rate, token-cost, anomalies (if any). Keep raw trace IDs for 50 random failures.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How aggressive should the token-cost gating be for latency-optimized models? Lowering it blocks useful rollouts. Proposal: use trailing 1h cost with 15-min smoothing. (action: discuss with finance next Wed).
- Do we want to add a "circuit-breaker" that temporarily reverts to a pinned model while keeping canary instances up for debugging? (Pros: faster investigation; Cons: complexity in routing)
- Add a multiline reason field to the pin/rollback API so the incident link + human summary attach automatically. (owner: Diego)

Postmortem/retrospective prompts (for after a rollout):
- What early signals were missed and why?
- Were automation thresholds too sensitive/lenient?
- Did the attenuation flow work without manual intervention? Latency of human ops?
- Any gaps in observability (missing tags, traces)?

Notes on experimentation and data capture:
- Always include deterministic seed in sample-run artifacts so offline diffs are reproducible. Label runs with commit and model hash.
- Keep a 'canary-artifacts' folder with a snapshot of token-level costs for the first 5000 requests. Helps correlate cost spikes with tokenization behavior.

Slack message templates (copyable snippets):
- Preflight ready: "rolling canary as-2026-03 to us-west1 at 0.5% (model redwood-7b-q2-opt-v3). Smoke checks passed in staging. Monitoring filters: rollout=as-safety-ladder. Will start at HH:MM PT. @channel"
- Attenuation auto: "Auto-attenuate applied to as-2026-03: -50% traffic due to p95 delta > 120ms. Investigating. Pager: @oncall"

Small personal TODO after this doc:
- Convert the most stable bits to a team runbook page in Confluence (link above).
- Add a short script to compile the per-rung metrics into a single CSV for archival.
- Pair with Diego on the pin API multiline reason field.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after next rollout.
